newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa higher on sterling weakness.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa higher on sterling weakness.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa moved higher in morning trade, helped by a weak sterling to buck traders' and analysts' expectations of a move lower.
By the midday break September was 13 stg higher at 1,014 stg.
September volume was 477 lots. December with 548 lots was more active. It last traded 11 stg higher at 1,044 stg. Total volume for the morning was 1,723 lots.
"We're looking for it to drift off," one trader said. But sterling's fall had created confusion, he said.
Darren Gurner, technical analyst at Sucden, took the same view. "The market is clearly in a bear trend," he said.
But a sharp sell-off in sterling offset the trend, traders said.

By midday Sterling was under 3.02 marks and below $1.60, standing four pfennigs and three cents below session highs. The foreign exchange market was nervously watching a Bank of England monetary policy meeting, which may agree a further rise in interest rates.
